title: zeroship.jsonc
description: The canonical creator project configuration. Read by the zeroship CLI and by the build toolchain; the file itself is NEVER read by the runtime or packed into a .zship. The build copies only runtime_date into the manifest, where it remains inert. See docs/reference/project-config.md.

$schema.description: Editor hint. Ignored by both readers.

name.description: The workspace name. Used as the app name when `zeroship deploy` auto-creates.

control.description: Control-plane base URL. There is NO Rust-side fallback: an absent key is an error naming the key, never a silent http://localhost:9090.

runtime_date.description: The scaffold stamps the current UTC date and the build carries it into the manifest. The runtime does not branch on it and no compatibility mechanism exists yet.

build.description: The build shape. `output` crosses the tool boundary (the packer writes it, `zeroship deploy` reads it); the rest is plugin-only.

databases.description: The workspace's databases, by LOCAL LABEL. A label is not resolvable: it names an entry in this map, and the CLI dereferences it to the entry's `id` before it makes any request, so a label never travels as an identifier. Declaring a database here grants nothing - `zeroship db bind` does, and deploy verifies the binding exists.

apps.description: The workspace's apps, by LOCAL LABEL. Each names the database labels it uses and which of them is its primary. `env.db` is the primary and `env.db === env.databases[primary]` by object identity.

secrets.description: Secret NAMES only. Values live in .env (dev) and `zeroship secret set` (deployed); deploy warns when a declared deployed value is absent. An array of strings has nowhere to put a value.

environments.description: Named deploy targets, selected with --env=<name>. There is no implicit environment and no ZEROSHIP_ENV fallback.

additionalProperties.description: `apps`, `control` and `databases` are NON-INHERITABLE, and each map must cover every label the root declares. An environment that names a production control and inherits a development database id lands WRITES in the wrong place, which is the cross-targeting this rule exists to prevent, one level worse than the wrong code. Everything else inherits, per member.

apps.description: One entry per root-declared app label, overriding its id. The LABEL is never overridden, so the manifest and the generated client are the same artifact across environments.

databases.description: One entry per root-declared database label, overriding its id. `migrations` and `out` are build-time paths and stay label-local.

protected.description: `zeroship migrate` against a protected environment requires --yes.

mode.description: "full" emits manifest.worker; "static" is an SSG-only deploy with no worker.

serverEntry.description: Server entry relative to the project root. Omit for auto-detection.

dist.description: The directory the client build writes, and the only directory the packer walks. The schema rejects the direct root and parent spellings; both readers additionally resolve the path and reject any directory containing zeroship.jsonc.

output.description: The .zship path the packer writes and `zeroship deploy` uploads. Both readers resolve it and reject the project root, an ancestor, a symlink, or an existing non-.zship path.

migrations.description: This database's migration sources, relative to the project root. The build folds them into <out>, and `zeroship migrate` records them into the request it posts.

out.description: The gen-types output dir holding env.db.ts and schema.runtime.json for THIS database. Both readers resolve it and reject the project root or an ancestor; the emitter refuses to overwrite unknown existing targets. Two databases may not share one, because the two filenames are fixed.

label.description: A creator-chosen LOCAL label. It is a map key, a member name on `env.databases`, and the only name a database has in the manifest, so it is constrained to what reads as one: lowercase, digits and underscores, starting with a letter. That excludes `__proto__` and every other inherited member name a plain property write could reach.

databaseId.description: The database's typed id. `zeroship db create` prints it. An identifier of real data, exactly as an app id is.

databases.description: The database LABELS this app uses. Every entry must name an entry of the workspace `databases` map. An empty array is a schema-less app: it gets no `env.db` at all.

primary.description: Which of `databases` is this app's primary, and therefore `env.db`. Required when `databases` is non-empty; refused when it is empty.

appId.description: The deploy target's app id. Absent on a fresh project: the first `zeroship deploy` auto-creates the app and writes its id here.
